core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Harim corresponds to the Arabic form حريم (Arabic root ح ر م (ḥ-r-m); حَرِيم (Ḥarīm)). Its core sense is intimate, innermost, sacred precinct. Harim is Arabic حَرِيم (Ḥarīm) 'a sacred/inviolable precinct, the women's quarters', from the root ح ر م (ḥ-r-m). The source gloss 'free from vows, pledges, or debts' is unsupported and belongs to a different root; it has been replaced with the lexical sense. Recorded at medium confidence because the source's Arabic column gave حارم, which is a different form. Same name as hareem.
